task_snapshots.title: Consolidate flask-restx model registration and extract URL validators
task_snapshots.description:
Two related quality issues in the API layer:

### 1. Triple-registered models
`add_models_to_api` in `app/models.py` builds and returns a fresh dict of models every time it is called. It is currently called THREE times: once from `app/__init__.py` on the top-level `Api`, once from `app/api/endpoints.py` on its `Namespace`, once from `app/api/settings.py` on its `Namespace`. Each call registers a new model instance — the objects that `endpoints.py:models["endpoint"]` and `__init__.py`s api models refer to are DIFFERENT objects. flask-restx tolerates this but it wastes work and makes the intent unclear.

### 2. URL validation lives in the API layer
`normalize_url` and `validate_url` are defined at the top of `app/api/endpoints.py`. They have no HTTP or Flask dependency and belong in a domain module so tests and future callers (e.g., a CLI) can reuse them.

## What to change
1. Refactor `app/models.py`:
   - Split `add_models_to_api` into two functions:
     - `build_models(api_or_ns)` — the existing body, unchanged (some flask-restx workflows need per-namespace registration for swagger discoverability, so preserve it as-is).
     - Add a module-level cache: `_MODELS: dict | None = None` and `def get_models(api) -> dict:` that lazily calls `build_models(api)` ONCE and returns the cached dict on subsequent calls.
   - Keep `add_models_to_api` as a thin alias for `build_models` for backwards compat with the two namespace files during migration.
2. Update `app/api/endpoints.py`:
   - Move `normalize_url` and `validate_url` (plus the inner `is_valid_ipv4`) to NEW file `app/core/validators.py`.
   - Import them: `from ..core.validators import normalize_url, validate_url`.
   - No behavior change; identical function bodies.
3. Update `app/api/settings.py`: no logic change needed unless it breaks — leave as-is (keeps its `add_models_to_api(ns)` call for now).
4. Create `app/core/validators.py` with the two functions (plus the inner helper made module-private as `_is_valid_ipv4`).

## Files you own
`app/models.py`, `app/api/endpoints.py`, `app/api/settings.py`, and NEW file `app/core/validators.py`. Nothing else. In particular, do NOT touch `app/__init__.py` (Task 5 owns it), `app/core/monitoring.py` (Task 3), `app/core/telegram_bot.py` (Task 4), `app/repositories/*` (Task 2), or `app/core/startup.py` (Task 5).

## Acceptance
- `app/core/validators.py` exists and exports `normalize_url`, `validate_url`.
- `grep -n "def normalize_url" app/api/endpoints.py` returns nothing.
- `grep -n "def validate_url" app/api/endpoints.py` returns nothing.
- `grep -n "def get_models" app/models.py` returns 1 match.
- `python -c "from app.core.validators import normalize_url, validate_url; assert validate_url(\"example.com\"); assert not validate_url(\"not a url with spaces\"); print(normalize_url(\"example.com\"))"` prints `https://example.com` and exits 0.
completion_signals: python -c "from app.core.validators import normalize_url, validate_url; assert validate_url(\"example.com\"); assert normalize_url(\"example.com\") == \"https://example.com\""
